questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?

options.text: Each of the players are given a trophy.
Every boy and girl have their task.
Either of the answers is acceptable.
Neither she nor her friends is ready.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Either of the answers is acceptable .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Option 3, **"Either of the answers is acceptable,"** is grammatically correct because the subject **"either"** is singular and requires a singular verb **"is."**
 
• Option 1, **"Each of the players are given a trophy,"** is incorrect because **"each"** is singular and should be followed by a singular verb **"is."**
 
• Option 2, **"Every boy and girl have their task,"** is incorrect because **"every"** is singular and should be followed by a singular verb **"has."**
 
• Option 4, **"Neither she nor her friends is ready,"** is incorrect because when using **"neither...nor"**, the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. In this case, **"friends"** is plural, so the correct verb would be **"are."**

Correct sentence: *Either of the answers **is acceptable**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agreement with Indefinite Pronouns:**

 
 
• Singular indefinite pronouns (e.g., **"each," "every," "either," "neither"**) take singular verbs.
 
• Example: Each of the students **has** completed their assignment.
 
 
 
• **Neither...Nor and Either...Or:**
 
 
• The verb agrees with the subject closest to it.
 
• Example: Neither the teacher nor the students **are** ready.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Identify Spot the error in the given sentence.

"The principal, along with the teachers, have approved the new syllabus."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. have approved should be replaced with **"has approved"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject of the sentence is **"The principal"**, which is singular.
 
• The phrase **"along with the teachers"** is additional information and does not affect the verb agreement.
 
• In subject-verb agreement, the verb should agree with the main subject of the sentence.
 
• The correct verb form for a singular subject like **"The principal"** is **"has"**, not **"have"**.

Correct sentence: *The principal, along with the teachers, **has approved** the new syllabus.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for Subject-Verb Agreement:**
 
 
• When the subject is singular, the verb must also be singular.
 
• When the subject is plural, the verb must also be plural.
 
• Parenthetical phrases like **"along with," "as well as," "in addition to"**, etc., do not affect the verb agreement.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• The teacher, along with the students, **is** preparing for the event.
 
• The manager, as well as the staff, **has** agreed to the new policy.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells an article at a discount of 12%. Had he given only a 5% discount, he would have earned ₹504 more as profit. If the cost price of the article is ₹3,000, then find the marked price.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price = 3000

Discount₁ = 12%

Discount₂ = 5%

Difference in profit = 504

**Formula Used:**

Selling price = Marked price × (100 − discount%) ÷ 100

Profit = Selling price − Cost price

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let Marked price = M

⇒ SP₁ = M × (88 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP₂ = M × (95 ÷ 100)

⇒ Profit difference = SP₂ − SP₁

⇒ 504 = M × (95 ÷ 100) − M × (88 ÷ 100)

⇒ 504 = M × (7 ÷ 100)

⇒ M = 504 × (100 ÷ 7)

⇒ M = 7200

**∴ The correct answer is 7200.**

⇒ 0.42 = (6d ÷ 100)

⇒ d = (0.42 × 100) ÷ 6 = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7%.**

• **To promote co-operative societies** is not mentioned among the Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A. *Hence, this option is correct.*

• The Fundamental Duties are not enforceable by law; however, they serve as moral obligations for citizens to uphold the spirit of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following bill provides details on the imposition, abolition, or regulation of taxes proposed in the budget?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Finance Bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Finance Bill** is a legislative proposal presented in Parliament along with the Union Budget to give effect to the financial proposals for the upcoming financial year.
 
• It contains provisions related to the **imposition, abolition, or alteration of taxes**, as proposed in the Union Budget.
 
• The Finance Bill is a **Money Bill** as per Article 110 of the Indian Constitution, meaning it is primarily concerned with taxation and government spending.
 
• The Bill needs to be passed by the Lok Sabha and can only be discussed but not amended by the Rajya Sabha, as per the provisions of the Constitution.
 
• The passage of the Finance Bill is crucial for implementing the financial proposals of the government, including tax amendments and budgetary allocations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Private Member Bill:**

 
 
• A Private Member Bill is introduced by a Member of Parliament who is not a minister.
 
• It is used to propose new laws or amendments to existing laws but is not related to financial matters.
 
• Only a small fraction of private member bills are passed in Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Constitution Amendment Bill:**
 
 
• This bill is introduced to amend the Constitution of India under Article 368.
 
• It requires a special majority in both Houses of Parliament and, in some cases, ratification by half of the state legislatures.
 
• It is not related to the imposition or abolition of taxes.
 
 
 
• **Ordinary Bill:**
 
 
• An Ordinary Bill is concerned with any matter other than financial or constitutional amendments.
 
• It can be introduced in either House of Parliament and does not require a special procedure for its passage.
 
• It is not used for tax-related proposals or budget implementation.
 
 
 
• **Money Bill:**
 
 
• A Money Bill is a subset of the Finance Bill and deals only with provisions mentioned in Article 110 of the Constitution, such as taxation, government borrowing, or expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India.
 
• It is certified as a Money Bill by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Finance Bill encompasses a broader scope than a Money Bill, including tax-related and non-tax-related financial proposals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Stages of the Finance Bill:**

 
 
• The Finance Bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha during the presentation of the Union Budget.
 
• It is debated and voted upon after the General Budget discussion is completed.
 
• The Bill must be passed within 75 days of its introduction, as per constitutional provisions.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Rajya Sabha:**
 
 
• The Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations to the Finance Bill but cannot amend or reject it.
 
• The Lok Sabha may accept or reject these recommendations.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Finance Bill and Appropriation Bill:**
 
 
• The Finance Bill deals with taxation and financial proposals, while the Appropriation Bill authorizes the government to withdraw funds from the Consolidated Fund of India.
 
• Both are essential for implementing the Union Budget.

questions.question:
As per the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management. Act-2003, the actual deficits may exceed the targets only on which of the following ground?

I. National security

II. National calamity
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 (FRBM Act)** was enacted by the Government of India to institutionalize financial discipline, reduce fiscal deficit, and improve macroeconomic management.
 
• As per the provisions of the FRBM Act, the central government is required to set annual targets to reduce fiscal deficits and eliminate revenue deficits.
 
• However, **Section 4(2) of the FRBM Act** provides for certain exceptions where the fiscal deficit targets can be exceeded. These are:
 
 
• **National Security:** In situations where national security is threatened, the government may breach the deficit target. This is deemed a valid exception. *Hence, Statement I is correct.*
 
• **National Calamity:** In the event of a severe national calamity (such as natural disasters), the government is allowed to exceed the prescribed fiscal deficit target to address the crisis effectively. *Hence, Statement II is correct.*
 
 
 
• The exceptions ensure that the government has the flexibility to respond to extraordinary circumstances without being constrained by fiscal deficit limits.
 
• It is important to note that these deviations must be approved by Parliament, and the government is required to present a detailed explanation for breaching the fiscal targets.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both I and II.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003:**

 
 
• The FRBM Act was enacted to ensure responsible fiscal management and achieve long-term macroeconomic stability.
 
• The Act includes measures such as reducing the fiscal deficit to a specified target (e.g., 3% of GDP) and eliminating the revenue deficit over time.
 
• The objective is to boost public savings, reduce inflationary pressures, and maintain sustainable debt levels.
 
• It applies to both the central government and state governments, although states have their own versions of FRBM laws.
 
 
 
• **Provisions for Deviation under FRBM Act:**
 
 
• Deviation from deficit targets is permissible under exceptional circumstances such as war, national security threats, natural calamities, or other extraordinary events.
 
• The government must provide a detailed explanation to Parliament when deviating from set targets, including measures to return to the prescribed path.
 
 
 
• **Amendments to the FRBM Act:**
 
 
• The Act has been amended several times, including the **2018 amendment**, which introduced a fiscal deficit glide path and mandated the establishment of a **Fiscal Council**.
 
• The fiscal deficit target was revised to a more flexible range, allowing for economic uncertainties.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic:**
 
 
• The fiscal rules under the FRBM Act were temporarily relaxed during the COVID-19 pandemic to allow the government to undertake higher spending to address the health and economic crisis.
 
• This highlighted the importance of having flexibility in fiscal management policies during emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• India's fiscal deficit for FY 2022-23 was projected at **6.4% of GDP**, reflecting higher government expenditure due to economic recovery measures.
 
• The FRBM Act emphasizes transparency and accountability in fiscal management by requiring the government to present fiscal policy statements and medium-term fiscal frameworks to Parliament.

questions.question:
Which Veda contains hymns mostly taken from the Rigveda, arranged for singing?

I. Samaveda

II. Yajurveda
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **The Samaveda** primarily consists of hymns and melodies that have been taken from the **Rigveda**. These hymns are specifically arranged for chanting and singing during rituals. 
• It is one of the four Vedas—**Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda**—and is regarded as the "Veda of melodies and chants." 
• The hymns of the Samaveda are chanted during **religious rituals and sacrifices** to invoke divine blessings. It is closely associated with the practice of **Soma rituals**. 
• Unlike the Rigveda, which focuses on the poetic aspect of hymns, the Samaveda emphasizes the **musical rendition** of these hymns, making it a unique collection of Vedic literature. 
• While many hymns in the Samaveda are borrowed from the Rigveda, their arrangement and purpose in the Samaveda are distinct, as they are meant to be sung rather than recited. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Rigveda:** 
• The Rigveda is the **oldest** of the four Vedas and consists of hymns that focus on the praise of various deities such as Agni, Indra, and Varuna. 
• It is written in **Sanskrit** and is considered one of the most ancient religious texts in the world. 
• The Rigveda contains a total of **1,028 hymns** divided into 10 books called Mandalas. 
• Its focus is on the poetic and philosophical aspects of Vedic literature. 
• **Yajurveda:** 
• The Yajurveda is primarily a compilation of **prose and verses** designed to guide the performance of rituals and sacrifices. 
• It is divided into two parts: the **Shukla (White) Yajurveda** and the **Krishna (Black) Yajurveda**. 
• Unlike the Samaveda, the Yajurveda focuses more on the procedural and practical aspects of conducting Vedic rituals. 
• **Atharvaveda:** 
• The Atharvaveda is considered the **Veda of knowledge** and includes hymns, spells, and incantations for practical purposes like healing, marriage, and protection against evils. 
• It is distinct from the other three Vedas in its focus on the everyday concerns of life rather than rituals. 
• **Samaveda's Unique Features:** 
• The Samaveda is often referred to as the "Book of Chants" due to its emphasis on **musical notations**. 
• It is regarded as the origin of Indian classical music and has had a profound influence on its development. 
• Priests who specialize in the Samaveda are called **Udgatris**, and they play a key role in chanting during rituals. 
• **Important Points:** 
• The **Samaveda** is closely associated with the **Sama Gana**, the singing style of Vedic hymns used during rituals. 
• It is especially used in **Soma Yajnas**, where Soma, a sacred plant, is offered to deities. 
• The Samaveda has contributed significantly to the cultural and spiritual heritage of India.
